# 03 The shapes drawn with a rect

## Outcome

`A(Round)`, `A([Stadium])` and `A[[Subroutine]]` draw the shapes they name.

## Why this ticket exists

Three shapes, one technique: still a `<rect>`, differing in corner radius or in an extra pair of
inner lines. Cheaper than tickets 01 and 02 precisely because the element does not change — which
makes one thing worth checking rather than assuming.

**The theme sets `rx: var(--siren-node-border-radius)` on `.siren-node-frame`.** For a plain
rectangle that is the rounded corner it has always drawn. A `round` node needs a *different*
radius, and a `stadium` needs `rx` equal to half its height. So this is the one ticket where the
shape and a documented theme token both want to set the same property, and the interaction has to
be decided rather than discovered.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] All three parse to their `NodeShape` and draw with the label fitting inside.
- [x] **Decide and state how a shape's radius and `--siren-node-border-radius` interact.** A
      stadium whose ends stop being semicircles because a consumer retuned the token is a bug; a
      `round` node that ignores the token entirely may be right or may be surprising. Say which you
      chose and why, and assert it — including what a consumer redeclaring the token gets.
- [x] A subroutine's inner lines are drawn and are part of the frame's styling story: an author's
      `style A fill:#f00` must not leave them looking detached. State what you did.
- [x] `A[[Subroutine]]`'s row leaves board 4's table (if ticket 02 did not already empty it).
- [x] Each shape still takes an author style and still animates.
- [x] Three corpus rows move to `supported`. `REJECTED` 26 → **23**; `SILENTLY_WRONG` untouched
      at **3**.

- [x] **The theme's coverage net is blind to your shapes until you widen it.**
      `theme/default.test.ts`'s "has a rule selecting every class the flowchart renderer emits"
      renders `EVERY_FLOWCHART_FEATURE`, which draws **only rectangles** — so a new `siren-*` class
      your shape emits would ship unthemed without failing anything. Add your shapes to that
      fixture if they emit any class the rect path does not, and say in your report whether they
      do. This matters most here because a multi-element frame is exactly where a second class
      gets invented.

- [x] **Found by ticket 02b.** `corpus.ts`'s `nodeStyle` and `nodeCenter` readers still query
      `rect.siren-node-frame`, so they silently return `""` or throw for a path-drawn node. No row
      uses them on a shaped node today, so nothing is wrong yet — but if you write a row that
      asserts styling or position on one of your shapes, widen them first rather than discovering
      it as a confusing empty string.

## On the ratchet numbers in this ticket

They are an **expectation, not a quota.** Ticket 01 found a real compatibility gap and declined to
fix it because adding a corpus row would have pushed `REJECTED` one above the number its ticket
named. That was an honest reading of a badly written instruction: the ratchet exists to stop
regressions, not to stop progress.

So: if you discover a gap, **add the row and say so**. `rejected` rising because a new gap was
measured is the same legitimate case as `silently-wrong` rising in board 4 — a measurement was
corrected, not code made worse. State which in your report, and move the literal to whatever the
suite actually produces.

## Status

Done (2026-09-07), commit 249cdfd. 8 slices (6 red-green, 2 written-after-code and bite-checked
by reverting the drawing while leaving `data-siren-shape` in place). 743 core tests / 29 board,
tsc clean both, both build. Ratchets: rejected 28 → **25** (exactly as expected — all three had
rows to leave), silently-wrong untouched at **3**.

**The radius decision**: a shape named for its corners owns them; the token rounds the shapes whose
corners are only decoration. Rect and subroutine take `--siren-node-border-radius`; round and
stadium write their own inline, so no token can flatten them — verified by the integrator.

Written as an inline declaration, not an `rx` attribute, because an attribute loses to any
stylesheet rule and the theme's own would have silently undone it.
